label: FDADSC: gabapentinoid with an opioid or sedative
title: Gabapentinoid with an opioid, benzodiazepine or Z-drug
statement: FDA is warning that serious breathing difficulties may occur in patients using gabapentin (Neurontin, Gralise, Horizant) or pregabalin (Lyrica, Lyrica CR) who have respiratory risk factors. These include the use of opioid pain medicines and other drugs that depress the central nervous system, and conditions such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease that reduce lung function. The elderly are also at higher risk. Health care professionals should start gabapentinoids at the lowest dose and monitor patients for symptoms of respiratory depression and sedation when co-prescribing gabapentinoids with an opioid or other central nervous system depressant such as a benzodiazepine.

plain_summary: Gabapentin or pregabalin with a systemic opioid, benzodiazepine or Z-drug can cause severe sedation and respiratory depression, including coma and death. This check requires a second medicine. The FDA also identifies reduced lung function, including from COPD, and older age as risk factors with a gabapentinoid. Neither alone triggers this check. No separate screening rule was found for those two situations. SCOTNTI-CNS-3 covers broader CNS polypharmacy. Australian TGA mandatory Boxed Warnings of 1 February 2021, Lyrica PI 2 November 2026 and Neurontin PI 17 September 2026 carry these warnings. Stilnox PI 21 May 2026 and Imovane PI 16 July 2026 align on additive sedation and respiratory risk.

medicine_groups.name: Systemic opioids, benzodiazepines and Z-drugs

codeine: Painstop for Children Day-Time Pain Reliever
Painstop for Children Night-Time Pain Reliever

medicine_groups.note: Systemic opioid analgesics count, including oxycodone with naloxone and buprenorphine analgesic products such as Norspan, B-Patch, Bupredermal and Temgesic. V2a sources: Australian Product Information and TGA register entries for these products. Benzodiazepines and the Z-drugs zolpidem and zopiclone count. Generic packs that show the ingredient name count too. Systemic buprenorphine and methadone count for pain or opioid dependence. This includes buprenorphine with naloxone.

rule_for_models: Review a gabapentin or pregabalin supply with a systemic opioid, benzodiazepine or Z-drug if the periods of use overlap or the supply dates are within 60 days. Cite one supply from each group. Report a finding for overlapping use, including opioids for dependence. Clearly separate courses give no finding. If use together is uncertain, including as-needed rescue treatment, report a possible finding and ask whether both were taken during the same period. Ask about sedation, breathing symptoms and respiratory risk factors such as COPD, other CNS depressants and older age.
cannot_be_seen: Supply dates do not prove that both medicines were taken together. The intentional scope is a gabapentinoid with a systemic opioid, benzodiazepine or Z-drug; broader multi-class CNS polypharmacy belongs to SCOTNTI-CNS-3. PRN use, sequential switches, other-pharmacy supplies, alcohol and non-prescription sedatives may be unclear. Actual sedation or breathing impairment is not shown.
ask_the_gp: A review of concurrent use, sedation and respiratory risk, and whether the lowest effective gabapentinoid dose and monitoring are in place.
